{
  "findings": [
    {
      "title": "Screening visit overloaded with many procedures",
      "quote": "Pulmonary function test | X |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |",
      "page": 18,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The screening visit includes a large number of procedures (e.g., pulmonary function test, tumor tissue sample, multiple blood samples, ECHO/MUGA, ophthalmologic assessments) all on Day -28, which may be burdensome for patients and sites.",
      "fix": "Consider spreading some assessments (e.g., pulmonary function test, ophthalmologic assessments) across the screening window or allow them to be done at a separate visit."
    },
    {
      "title": "Tumor tissue sample at progression may be difficult to collect",
      "quote": "Tumor tissue sample taken at pre- treatment, on-treatment,and at disease progression (optional, only if part of the SoC) | X |  |  |  |  |  |  | X |",
      "page": 18,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "Collecting a tumor tissue sample at disease progression is often challenging in practice, even if optional, and may add burden to patients and sites.",
      "fix": "Clarify that this is optional and consider waiving if not clinically indicated; provide clear instructions for sites on how to handle if not feasible."
    },
    {
      "title": "Multiple blood samples on C1D1 may be excessive",
      "quote": "Blood sample for plasma biomarker assessment and diagnostic development(eg, ctDNA and blood- based biomarkers) (mandatory) | X | X |  |  | X | X |  | X |",
      "page": 18,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "On Cycle 1 Day 1, there are multiple mandatory blood samples (plasma biomarker, gene expression, exploratory, PK pre-dose, PK post-dose, ADA) which may be burdensome and require multiple draws.",
      "fix": "Consolidate blood draws where possible or reduce the number of mandatory samples on the same day."
    },
    {
      "title": "PK sampling at post-dose on C1D1 and C2D1 may be logistically challenging",
      "quote": "Post-dose blood sample for T-DXd PK (serum) (T-DXd, total anti-HER2 antibody & MAAA-1181) |  | X |  |  | X |  |  | X |",
      "page": 18,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "Post-dose PK samples require precise timing relative to infusion, which can be difficult to coordinate in busy clinical settings, especially on the same day as other procedures.",
      "fix": "Provide clear instructions for PK sampling windows and consider allowing flexibility in timing or using a separate visit for PK if needed."
    },
    {
      "title": "Tumor assessments only at screening and not repeated during treatment",
      "quote": "Tumor assessments (RECIST v1.1) | X |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |",
      "page": 18,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "critical",
      "explanation": "Tumor assessments are only listed at screening, with no on-treatment or end-of-treatment tumor assessments, which is inconsistent with standard oncology trials and would not allow evaluation of response.",
      "fix": "Add tumor assessments at regular intervals during treatment (e.g., every 6-8 weeks) and at end of treatment."
    },
    {
      "title": "High Resolution Chest CT only at screening",
      "quote": "High Resolution Chest CT | X |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |",
      "page": 18,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "critical",
      "explanation": "High Resolution Chest CT is only performed at screening, but it should be repeated during treatment to monitor for lung toxicity, especially with T-DXd which has known interstitial lung disease risk.",
      "fix": "Add High Resolution Chest CT at specified intervals during treatment and at end of treatment."
    },
    {
      "title": "Ophthalmologic assessments only at screening and EOT may miss on-treatment events",
      "quote": "Ophthalmologic Assessments | X |  |  |  |  |  |  | X |",
      "page": 18,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "Ophthalmologic assessments are only at screening and end of treatment, which may miss ocular toxicities that occur during treatment; also, these assessments can be burdensome and require specialist visits.",
      "fix": "Consider adding ophthalmologic assessments at regular intervals during treatment if there is a known risk, or clarify that they are only needed if symptoms occur."
    },
    {
      "title": "ePRO and pulse oximetry device allocation on C1D1 may be burdensome",
      "quote": "ePRO and pulse oximetry device allocation (ePRO device allocated only if patient does not have own compatible device) and trainingu |  | X |  |  |  |  |  |  |",
      "page": 18,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "Allocating and training on ePRO and pulse oximetry devices on Cycle 1 Day 1, which is already a heavy visit with dosing and many assessments, may be overwhelming for patients and staff.",
      "fix": "Consider providing device training during screening or a separate visit to reduce burden on C1D1."
    }
  ]
}
